items.title: Top-level family identity and closure are explicit
items.statement: Both values have stable family/schema identities, fixed schema versions, canonical encoding, and closed top-level object schemas. This is an explicit non-gap for coarse decoding and rejection of unknown top-level fields.

items.title: Intake status has no conditional invariants
items.statement: The schema permits rejected or blocked reports without a corresponding reason, accepted reports with rejected/blocked reasons, and accepted_at_utc on any status. It therefore cannot falsify contradictory intake states or define the allowed transition from preflight to acceptance.
items.impact: Consumers can render or certify mutually contradictory intake truth.
items.builder_discretion: Specify if/then constraints for every status, reason presence/nullability, and acceptance time, plus legal transition or immutability semantics.

items.title: Preflight domain results are unconstrained objects
items.statement: Every required preflight domain result is only typed as object. The contract defines no pass/fail state, reason code, evidence binding, schema identity, or nested closure, so graph, source-control, test, routing, authority, readiness, and scheduler outcomes cannot be validated or consistently interpreted.
items.impact: Malformed, contradictory, or empty domain results satisfy the registry while consumers infer different readiness and authority truth.
items.builder_discretion: Define a shared closed result envelope and domain-specific payload/oracles, including explicit status, evidence refs, and stable reason codes.

items.title: Runtime-disabled replay guard is prose-only
items.statement: The replay rule says intake replay must not launch activation while runtime is disabled, but the value has no runtime-mode snapshot, guard decision, activation eligibility, policy version, or executable invariant. A consumer cannot prove from this record that replay remained non-activating.
items.impact: Replay code can accidentally cross the disabled-runtime authority boundary while still accepting a schema-valid report.
items.builder_discretion: Bind the report to a machine-checkable runtime gate decision and policy/version evidence, and define replay rejection behavior when it is absent or stale.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay uses the report to explain accepted/rejected/blocked intake without launching activation when runtime is disabled.",

items.title: Key/value binding and concurrent-write semantics are absent
items.statement: The keys embed project/request/intake or project/attempt/receipt identities, but value identifiers are merely non-empty strings and are not declared equal to the key components. Neither family defines create-only, compare-and-swap, revision, idempotency, duplicate, stale-writer, or conflict behavior.
items.impact: Cross-project misbinding, duplicate writes, or last-writer-wins races can silently replace authoritative intake or receipt truth.
items.builder_discretion: Define key/value equality validation, immutable/create-only behavior or explicit revision CAS, idempotency keys, and deterministic conflict outcomes.

items.title: Redaction assertions conflict with arbitrary nested content
items.statement: Both families declare that secrets and raw provider output are not stored, yet preflight results and result_summary are arbitrary objects and refs are unrestricted strings. redaction_profile is self-asserted rather than backed by field-level schema, sanitizer version, or validation evidence.
items.impact: Credentials, sensitive repository content, provider output, or personal data can be persisted in a schema-valid record and propagated to GUI/audit consumers.
items.builder_discretion: Close every nested payload, constrain ref schemes, record sanitizer/profile version and redaction proof, and reject unknown sensitive fields before persistence.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Preflight details are result refs and status objects; no repository secret, auth token, or local credential is stored.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Receipt stores artifact/evidence refs and redacted summaries only, not raw provider output or credentials.",

items.title: Retention and deletion lifecycle is underspecified
items.statement: Retention is expressed only as reachability prose. There is no duration, deletion/tombstone protocol, reference-count race behavior, legal-hold or user-deletion rule, encryption lifecycle, secure compaction guarantee, or handling for a parent deleted before dependent receipts.
items.impact: Records can be deleted too early, retained indefinitely, or leave sensitive bytes in compacted storage without a testable lifecycle outcome.
items.builder_discretion: Specify lifecycle states, durations and holds, dependency ordering, tombstones, compaction erasure expectations, and deletion receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain with the parent WorkNodeRequest and any blocked/goal receipts that cite the intake id.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain canonical receipts and evidence refs; compact only derived summaries once source receipts remain reachable.",

items.title: Migration rules lack mappings and failure behavior
items.statement: One family declares old reports invalid and the other says aliases migrate, but neither specifies source versions, field mappings, deterministic defaults, quarantine, rollback, partial-batch behavior, collision handling, provenance, or validation oracles.
items.impact: Upgrade/replay can silently drop historical evidence, synthesize incompatible receipts, or strand records with no recoverable migration path.
items.builder_discretion: Provide versioned migration tables, deterministic converters, provenance, dry-run/rollback, per-record failure receipts, and post-migration invariants.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Reports lacking schema_version or per-domain result objects are invalid for Executor intake replay.",
"migration": "Older receipt aliases migrate into attempt_receipt with explicit schema_version, source refs, and redaction profile.",

items.title: Attempt status is not a lifecycle contract
items.statement: The receipt enumerates terminal-looking statuses but defines neither legal transitions nor immutability. superseded has no required replacement reference, failed/blocked/cancelled have no required reason, and completed has no required success/evidence conditions.
items.impact: A schema-valid receipt can claim completion without proof or become superseded without a traceable successor.
items.builder_discretion: Define receipt immutability or a transition graph and add status-discriminated reason, successor, completion, and evidence requirements.

items.title: Required reference arrays may be empty, duplicate, or invalid
items.statement: Source, destination, evidence, and validator arrays are required but have no minItems, uniqueItems, item minLength, ref grammar, existence/integrity requirement, or status-dependent cardinality. Empty arrays and empty-string entries therefore satisfy the schema.
items.impact: Goal certification and audit projection can consume receipts that carry no evidence, no validators, or dangling/ambiguous artifacts.
items.builder_discretion: Constrain ref format and uniqueness, define required cardinality by receipt kind/status, and bind refs to existence/hash/access checks.

items.title: Retry and rollback routes are untyped destructive-action strings
items.statement: retry_route and rollback_route are mandatory arbitrary strings while safe_point_id is optional and nullable. There is no route schema, target, authorization, precondition, idempotency, retry budget, compensation result, rollback scope, approval, or distinction between no-op and destructive rollback.
items.impact: Automated recovery can invoke an unsafe or stale route, repeat destructive work, or claim rollback without a recoverable safe point or recorded outcome.
items.builder_discretion: Use closed route objects bound to attempt/run/safe-point identity, authority and preconditions; define idempotent execution, budgets, compensation receipts, and failure escalation.

items.title: Receipt authenticity and authority provenance are absent
items.statement: The receipt records no producer identity, actor/principal, authority decision, policy version, signature/MAC, immutable digest, or trust domain. Merely naming an Executor receipt writer as producer does not let consumers authenticate who created or authorized a receipt.
items.impact: A forged or cross-project receipt can drive Goal Runtime certification, GUI truth, recovery routes, or audit evidence without a verifiable authority chain.
items.builder_discretion: Bind producer/principal/policy and trust domain to the record and require integrity/authenticity verification before privileged consumers accept it.

items.title: Caller and cross-document linkage is incomplete
items.statement: The attempt receipt lists GUI, certification, and audit consumers but no retry/rollback executor, artifact lifecycle manager, evidence resolver, validator resolver, migration worker, or retention/deletion owner. It also omits request_id and intake_id, leaving the seam from executor_intake_report to the attempt only through an opaque execution_unit_context_ref.
items.impact: Critical routes and refs can be unowned, and Goal Runtime cannot deterministically join preflight intake truth to execution receipts.
items.builder_discretion: Name every lifecycle consumer/owner and add explicit typed linkage among request, intake, run, node, attempt, and receipt identities.

items.title: GUI-facing truth lacks structured, localizable, accessible semantics
items.statement: Runtime Artifacts is a named consumer, but result_summary is an arbitrary object and reason/risk strings have no stable message code, argument schema, severity, user-action, provenance, safe-display marker, locale-neutral semantics, or accessible state description. The panel can therefore overstate completion or expose raw technical text.
items.impact: Users, including assistive-technology users, may receive contradictory, untranslated, unsafe, or non-actionable status while the stored receipt remains schema-valid.
items.builder_discretion: Define stable machine codes plus typed message parameters, display severity/actionability/provenance, safe-display/redaction state, and a UI mapping oracle independent of locale.

items.title: Opaque refs and routes are untrusted-input surfaces
items.statement: Context, provider, usage, worktree, artifact, evidence, validator, retry, and rollback references are unrestricted strings. The contract defines no scheme allowlist, canonicalization, project namespace, traversal/URL policy, maximum length, existence check, or dereference authorization.
items.impact: Malicious or malformed refs can trigger path traversal, SSRF-like dereference, cross-project disclosure, confusing alias resolution, or unsafe route execution.
items.builder_discretion: Use typed closed ref objects with allowed schemes, normalized identifiers, namespace binding, length limits, hashes, and authorization at dereference time.

items.title: Objects, arrays, strings, and receipt fan-out are unbounded
items.statement: Arbitrary result objects and all reference/risk arrays lack maximum serialized size, nesting depth, item count, item length, or compaction thresholds. Key cardinality and per-attempt receipt limits are also unspecified.
items.impact: A valid value can exhaust memory/storage, stall MessagePack decoding or GUI projection, amplify audit work, and deny service through receipt fan-out.
items.builder_discretion: Set byte/depth/count/string/cardinality limits, reject oversize records atomically, and define bounded pagination/compaction and overload telemetry.

items.title: Write durability, partial failure, and support telemetry are undefined
items.statement: created_at_utc is the only temporal field. There is no write transaction boundary across value/index/projections, commit sequence, attempt ordinal, updated/finalized time, trace/correlation id, producer build, checksum, write failure receipt, recovery scan, stale projection marker, or offline/crash replay rule.
items.impact: After crash, disk-full, offline provider, or partial projector failure, support cannot distinguish committed truth from a stale/duplicate/partially propagated receipt or deterministically repair it.
items.builder_discretion: Define atomic commit/outbox boundaries, monotonic sequencing, crash recovery and idempotent projection, plus trace/build/checksum and partial-failure telemetry.

items.title: Receipt summaries are explicitly denied activation-proof authority
items.statement: The receipt replay rule explicitly says summaries are not executable activation proof, and retention explicitly preserves canonical receipts/evidence reachability before derived-summary compaction. These are useful negative-authority and evidence-preservation non-gaps, though enforcement details remain open in other findings.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay joins attempt receipts by project/attempt/receipt and never treats receipt summaries as executable activation proof.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain canonical receipts and evidence refs; compact only derived summaries once source receipts remain reachable.",

items.title: Unconstrained blobs hide unknown downstream semantics
items.statement: Because seven preflight results and result_summary accept any object, the window does not reveal their nested authority, failure, privacy, compatibility, or test semantics. This is an explicit unknown rather than evidence that those dimensions are safely handled elsewhere.
items.impact: Critical behavior can be smuggled into undocumented nested shapes and become de facto contract through consumer implementation.
items.builder_discretion: Inventory actual producers/consumers and replace opaque objects with versioned closed schemas before treating the families as buildable.

dimension_assessments.summary: Retry/rollback execution, artifact/evidence resolution, migration, and retention ownership are not represented among consumers, and intake-to-attempt linkage is opaque.
Neither intake nor attempt status has conditional field invariants, legal transitions, or explicit immutability/supersession semantics.
Key/value equality, create-only or revision CAS, duplicate/idempotency, stale-writer, and multi-projection commit behavior are undefined.
The schema lacks atomic write/projector boundaries, partial-failure receipts, recovery scans, and evidence cardinality sufficient to detect incomplete records.
Retry and rollback are arbitrary strings without typed targets, safe-point requirements, idempotency, budgets, outcomes, or escalation.
Runtime replay guards are prose-only, preflight authority results are opaque, and receipts have no authenticated producer/principal/policy provenance.
Self-asserted redaction coexists with arbitrary objects/refs, while deletion, retention duration, holds, encryption, and secure compaction are unspecified.
Opaque refs, routes, result objects, and summaries lack grammar, normalization, namespace, size, integrity, and dereference-authorization constraints.
The Runtime Artifacts panel can receive completed receipts with empty evidence and arbitrary summaries lacking provenance, risk severity, and safe-display semantics.
No offline/crash durability, transactional outbox, deterministic duplicate handling, stale projection, or recovery replay behavior is defined.
Nested objects, arrays, strings, values, and per-attempt receipt cardinality are unbounded.
The GUI-facing receipt lacks structured state, severity, actionability, and safe user-description fields from which consistent accessible status can be derived.
Reasons, risks, routes, and summaries lack stable locale-neutral message codes and typed interpolation arguments.
Migration prose defines neither version mappings nor deterministic failure, collision, rollback, provenance, and post-migration validation behavior.
Created time alone cannot support correlation, sequence reconstruction, producer/build diagnosis, integrity verification, partial-write detection, or repair.
Rollback routes have no approval, scope, precondition, safe-point requirement, idempotency, compensation result, or destructive/no-op classification.
The storage seam does not explicitly join request/intake identities to run/node/attempt/receipt identities or define lifecycle owners for refs and routes.
Opaque result objects, empty evidence arrays, prose-only guards, and missing status discriminators prevent deterministic acceptance and failure oracles.
The arbitrary nested result/summary objects hide semantics not inspectable in this authoritative window; their safety cannot be inferred.
